questions.question: 1. Selection sort has the same average-case time complexity as worst-case time complexity.

explanations.a: Correct. Selection sort always performs O(N^2) comparisons regardless of the initial order of elements, so both average and worst-case time complexity are the same.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Selection sort does have the same time complexity for both average and worst cases.

questions.question: 2. In which case can selection sort be used?

answers.a: For a fast and efficient sorting

explanations.a: Incorrect. Selection sort is not fast with O(N^2) time complexity.
explanations.b: Correct. Selection sort is memory efficient as it sorts in-place with O(1) auxiliary space and performs minimal swaps.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Selection sort requires comparisons to find the minimum element.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Selection sort is useful for memory efficient sorting.

questions.question: 3. Pick the incorrect step in selection sorting.

answers.a: Find the smallest element with the least index, such that index≤i≤N-1.
answers.b: Swap the element at index i with the element at index i+1.
answers.c: Swap the smallest element found with the element at index i.

explanations.a: Incorrect. This is a correct step in selection sort.
explanations.b: Correct. This is incorrect because we swap the smallest element with the element at index i, not with i+1.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is a correct step in selection sort.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Option b is an incorrect step.

questions.question: 4. What are the correct intermediate steps when you perform Selection Sort on [2, 7, -3, 5]?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This skips an intermediate step.
explanations.b: Correct. First swap -3 with 2: [-3, 7, 2, 5]. Then swap 2 with 7: [-3, 2, 7, 5]. Finally swap 5 with 7: [-3, 2, 5, 7].
explanations.c: Incorrect. This does not follow the selection sort process correctly.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This does not follow the selection sort process correctly.

questions.question: 5. How many loops are there in the selection sort code?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Selection sort uses two nested loops: one for the current position and one for finding the minimum.
explanations.b: Correct. Selection sort uses two nested loops: the outer loop for each position and the inner loop to find the minimum element.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The loops are nested, not separate.
explanations.d: Incorrect. There are not three loops in selection sort.
